header:
A Solvent-Responsive Color-Changing Complex
The pentacyanoferrate(II) complex ion X is a solvatochromic complex that is highly sensitive to changes in the dielectric constant and hydrogen-bond-donor ability of its solvent environment. Studies show that the color of X changes in opposite directions with solvent composition in the two binary solvent systems methanol/water and formamide (FA)/water.

subquestions.text_open:
2.1 The color of complex ion X arises primarily from metal-to-ligand charge transfer, MLCT.
2.1.2 In the MLCT mechanism of X, the excited state $X^{*}$ can be represented by a limiting resonance form of the ground-state ion in which one nitrogen atom of the organic ligand is a radical cation. Write the SMILES string of this limiting resonance form and correctly label the oxidation state of Fe.

text_images.description: X has the SMILES 'COC(C=C1)=CC=C1[N+](C=C2)=CC=C2C3=CC=[N]([Fe+2]([C-]#N)([C-]#N)([C-]#N)([C-]#N)[C-]#N)C=C3'. Complex ion X has an overall charge of two negative units.

subquestions.text_open: 2.1.3 State which has the larger dipole moment: ground-state X or its excited state $X^{*}$.

2.2 To quantify the effects of solvent dielectric constant and hydrogen-bond-donor ability on the color of the complex ion, the following linear relationship is used:
$E_{CT} = E_0 + s\cdot f(ε) + k\cdot α$
where ε is the dielectric constant of the solvent, α is the hydrogen-bond-donor acidity of the solvent, the Onsager polarity function is $f(ε)=\frac{2(ε-1)}{2ε+1}$, and s and k are the corresponding linear coefficients.
2.2.3 For a binary methanol/water solvent, the fitted linear coefficients are
$E_0$ = −28.112 kcal·mol^{-1}; s = 123.758 kcal·mol^{-1}; k = −61.985 kcal·mol^{-1}.
The dielectric constant ε of the binary methanol/water solvent is approximately linearly related to the mole fraction of methanol $x_{MeOH}$:
$ε = 79.2 - 43.6\cdot x_{MeOH}$
The hydrogen-bond-donor acidity α of the mixed solvent is approximately independent of solvent composition. Calculate the slope of $E_{CT}$ with respect to $x_{MeOH}$ for the complex in the mixed solvent at $x_{MeOH}$ = 0.50. Hint: for $u = u(v(x))$, $du/dx = (du/dv) \cdot (dv/dx)$.

2.3 In a binary formamide (FA)/water solvent, FA is the more polar component. Preferential solvation makes the local solvent mole fraction y around the solute differ from the bulk solvent mole fraction x. The Suppan dielectric-enrichment model is used:
$\frac{y_n}{y_p}=\frac{x_n}{x_p}e^{-Z_{ps}}$
where the subscript n denotes the less polar solvent and p the more polar solvent. In an FA/water mixture, the solvation index is $Z_{ps}=0.412$.
2.3.2 Define the local enrichment factor of the more polar solvent p as $η_p = y_p / x_p$. Derive an expression for $η_p$ in terms of $x_p$ and $Z_{ps}$, and calculate $η_p$ at $x_p$ = 0.600.

Experimental observation: in methanol/water, the absorption peak shifts to the blue as the mole fraction of the more polar component, water, increases. In FA/water, the absorption peak shifts to the red as the mole fraction of the more polar component, FA, increases, and preferential solvation occurs.
